scope.completeness: Not a manual handbook-image extraction or exhaustive per-card semantic audit; misses and false positives are possible. Sources, currentness and accuracy remain subject to independent review.
scope.current_observation: Proposed needs only; absence or presence of an existing image is not asserted.

asset_policy.signs: Use accurate authoritative sign artwork only after verifying local applicability and reuse rights; do not invent signs.

method.classification_caveat: Keyword rules can overmatch, miss topics, or classify a text rule as visual recognition. Manual review is required.

method.coverage_note: Only accepted card files listed in the pinned manifest were scanned; unmatched cards remain unreviewed and may need images.

source_cards.back: A child restraint must bear a sticker showing compliance with the federal child-restraint standard.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for secured child restraint?
source_cards.back: A child restraint must be permanently secured to the vehicle or attached using a safety belt or attachment system.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for rear facing seat and air bag?
source_cards.back: A rear-facing child seat must never be placed in the front passenger position when that position has an air bag.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for rear facing infant seat?
source_cards.back: An infant seat must face toward the rear of the vehicle.

needs.title: Skid and traction recovery

source_cards.front: What is the rule for hydroplaning?
source_cards.back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water instead of contacting the road and depends on water, road conditions and speed.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for hydroplaning response?

source_cards.front: What is the rule for icy skid response?
source_cards.back: Locking the brakes on ice causes loss of steering control, and a skid calls for steering in the skid’s direction.

needs.title: Visibility and road hazards in weather

source_cards.front: What is the rule for initial rain slickness?
source_cards.back: Slow when rain first begins because water can mix with road dirt and oil into a slippery film.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for icy skid response?
source_cards.back: Locking the brakes on ice causes loss of steering control, and a skid calls for steering in the skid’s direction.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for clear the entire vehicle?
source_cards.back: Remove all snow and ice from the vehicle, including the roof, hood and trunk, so it cannot blow onto vehicles behind.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for snow removal liability?
source_cards.back: Failing to remove snow and ice from the vehicle can result in a negligent-operation charge.

needs.title: Motorcycle road position and visibility

source_cards.front: What is the rule for motorcycle road rights?
source_cards.back: A motorcycle is a motor vehicle with the same roadway rights as a car or truck.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for full motorcycle lane?
source_cards.back: A motorcycle is entitled to the entire lane, and another vehicle must not share its lane space.

needs.title: Passing and no-passing situations

source_cards.front: What is the rule for passing clearance?
source_cards.back: Leave at least four feet of safe clearance when passing a vulnerable road user.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for safe passing lane use?
source_cards.back: When safe, a driver passing a vulnerable road user may use the adjacent lane and cross the center line if needed, while still obeying the speed limit.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for no pressure at blind crossing?
source_cards.back: Do not honk at a blind pedestrian, wave the person across or pass a vehicle stopped for that crossing.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for slow rider pass?
source_cards.back: Slow when passing a bicycle or moped because vehicle-generated wind can upset the rider’s balance.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for scooter keep right rule?
source_cards.back: A motorized-scooter operator must stay on the road’s right side even when passing another vehicle.

needs.title: Crosswalks and stop positions

source_cards.front: What is the rule for flashing red stop position?
source_cards.back: At flashing red, stop before a marked stop line or crosswalk; without a line, stop where you can see traffic before entering the intersection.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for no yellow start?
source_cards.back: A driver already stopped at an intersection or stop line must not start through on steady yellow.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for countdown does not remove right of way?
source_cards.back: A pedestrian already in a crosswalk retains right of way after the pedestrian countdown reaches zero.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for crosswalk yielding?
source_cards.back: Drivers must yield to pedestrians entering or using a crosswalk in the vehicle’s path.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for keep crosswalk clear?
source_cards.back: A vehicle must never block a crosswalk.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for pedestrian crossing facility?
source_cards.back: Pedestrians must use an available crosswalk and request the WALK phase with the button where one exists.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for complete stop position?
source_cards.back: A Stop sign requires every approaching vehicle to halt completely before any stop line or crosswalk.

needs.title: Traffic and pedestrian signals

source_cards.front: What is the rule for Massachusetts red arrow?
source_cards.back: In Massachusetts a steady red arrow applies the round-red rules to vehicles traveling in its direction, including the same permitted-turn-on-red rules.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for flashing red?
source_cards.back: A flashing red signal requires the same complete stop and safe yielding as a stop sign.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for steady yellow?
source_cards.back: A steady yellow signal announces the change from green to red and requires stopping when safe.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for flashing yellow?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow signal calls for caution, alertness and checking both directions at an intersection.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for flashing arrow gap?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow arrow permits a turn in its direction only after the driver finds a sufficient oncoming-traffic gap and a clear pedestrian path.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for left on green?
source_cards.back: A driver turning left on a steady green signal must yield to oncoming traffic.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for protected green arrow?
source_cards.back: A green arrow permits a protected turn in the arrow’s direction, with pedestrians and opposing traffic expected to face red.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for blacked out signal?
source_cards.back: A completely dark nonfunctioning traffic signal is treated cautiously as an all-way stop.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for red pedestrian yielding?
source_cards.back: A driver must yield to pedestrians when facing a red signal or a red-and-yellow signal.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for no red light turn?
source_cards.back: A No Turn on Red sign prohibits the indicated turn after stopping at a red signal.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for electronic tolling guide?

source_cards.front: What is the rule for regulatory messages?

source_cards.front: What is the rule for green highway guidance?

needs.title: Turning paths and lanes

source_cards.front: What is the rule for right on red conditions?
source_cards.back: A right turn on red is allowed only after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and other traffic, and is forbidden when a No Turn on Red sign is posted.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for one way left on red?
source_cards.back: A left turn on red is allowed from a one-way street onto another one-way street after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for left on green?
source_cards.back: A driver turning left on a steady green signal must yield to oncoming traffic.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for prohibited turn arrows?
source_cards.back: A crossed-out right-turn arrow prohibits a right turn, and a crossed-out left-turn arrow prohibits a left turn.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for turn versus curve cue?
source_cards.back: A sharp right-angle arrow warns of a right turn, while a curved right arrow warns of a right curve.

source_cards.back: The regulatory sign chart opens with Yield alongside turn and road-user prohibitions covering right turns, left turns, U-turns, trucks, pedestrians, and bicycles.

source_cards.front: Which pedestrian warning signs appear in the warning sign chart?
source_cards.back: The warning sign chart includes both pedestrian crossing signs and a pedestrian crossing ahead sign.

source_cards.front: How does the warning sign chart list added-lane and merging-lane warnings?
source_cards.back: The warning sign chart shows an added lane warning sign separately from the sign for a lane merging from the right, which tells drivers to watch for other traffic.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for crossbuck and track count?
source_cards.back: A white crossbuck marks where tracks cross the road, and a plaque below gives the track count when there is more than one.

needs.title: Sharing lanes and space with bicycles

source_cards.front: What is the rule for sharrow purpose?
source_cards.back: Shared-lane markings help bicyclists choose position and direction in a lane shared with motor vehicles.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for sharrow versus bicycle lane?
source_cards.back: A sharrow calls for watching for bicyclists and allowing passing room, and is different from a bicycle-lane marking.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for crossing a bicycle lane?
source_cards.back: Motor vehicles may drive in a bicycle lane only to turn onto or off the road and must check carefully for bicycles before crossing.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for advisory bicycle lane?
source_cards.back: Dashed advisory bicycle lanes allow motor vehicles to use that space when necessary only after yielding to bicyclists.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for intersection bicycle check?
source_cards.back: Before proceeding at an intersection, look twice for bicycles and allow ample space.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for left turn yielding?
source_cards.back: Before any left turn, yield to approaching traffic, vehicles already in the intersection and pedestrians or bicyclists crossing the turn path.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for entering paved road?
source_cards.back: Before entering a paved through road from a private road, driveway or unpaved road, stop and yield to pedestrians, bicycles and vehicles on that road.

needs.title: Vehicle blind spots

source_cards.front: What is the rule for look signal move?
source_cards.back: Before turning, merging, entering traffic or changing lanes, check mirrors and the relevant blind spot, then signal and move.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for avoid blind spot travel?
source_cards.back: Avoid lingering in another driver’s blind spot and pass through it safely as promptly as possible.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for large vehicle blind spots?
source_cards.back: Large vehicles have blind spots at the sides, front and rear, so avoid driving immediately around them or following a truck or bus closely.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for shoulder travel exit check?
source_cards.back: Before exiting where breakdown-lane travel is allowed, check to the right and inspect the right blind spot.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for turn preparation?
source_cards.back: Before turning, slow down, check mirrors and the turning-side blind spot and yield where required.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for three point turn setup?
source_cards.back: Before a three-point turn, move near the right curb, signal left, check traffic and pedestrians both ways including the blind spot and wait for a twenty-to-thirty-second gap.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for reverse turning movement?
source_cards.back: For the reversing portion of a three-point turn, turn the wheel fully right, check traffic and blind spots and back while looking over the right shoulder.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for final turning movement?
source_cards.back: To finish the three-point turn, recheck both directions and blind spots, signal left, select drive or first gear and accelerate to the appropriate speed.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for controlled backing?
source_cards.back: For ordinary backing, begin near the right curb, check both directions and blind spots, then reverse while looking over the right shoulder at a safe smooth speed within the lane.

source_cards.back: When a vehicle's electronic signals are not working, drivers must give the required left-turn hand signal through the driver's side window.

source_cards.front: How must a driver give a right-turn hand signal when electronic signals fail?
source_cards.back: When a vehicle's electronic signals are not working, drivers must give the required right-turn hand signal through the driver's side window, and road-test applicants must know all three hand signals.

source_cards.front: How do drivers and bicyclists give hand signals when slowing or stopping?
source_cards.back: When a vehicle's electronic signals are not working, drivers must give the hand signal for slowing or stopping through the driver's side window, whereas bicyclists may signal with either arm.

source_cards.back: A solid white or yellow line that becomes short dotted dashes continues the line through an intersection or interchange.

source_cards.back: White lines separate traffic traveling in the same direction and can mark the right pavement edge.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for broken white crossing?

source_cards.back: Crossing double solid white lines separating same-direction lanes is prohibited.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for mixed yellow lines?
source_cards.back: With paired solid and broken yellow lines, a driver beside the solid line may not cross, while a driver beside the broken line may cross for a safe pass.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for double yellow passing prohibition?
source_cards.back: Two solid yellow lines prohibit crossing to pass another vehicle.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for white lane arrows?

source_cards.front: What is the rule for left turn yielding?

source_cards.back: Never use the shoulder, breakdown lane or sidewalk to pass a vehicle.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for passing lanes?

source_cards.front: What is the rule for passing preparation?

source_cards.front: What is the rule for passing signals?

source_cards.front: What is the rule for return lane clearance?
source_cards.back: Before returning right after a pass, wait at least until the passed vehicle’s headlights can be seen in the mirror and sufficient room exists.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for permitted right passes?
source_cards.back: Subject to the clear-and-wide-road condition, passing on the right is allowed beside a vehicle turning left or on a one-way street or same-direction roadway.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for longer large vehicle pass?
source_cards.back: Passing a tractor-trailer or bus takes longer than passing a smaller vehicle, and large vehicles may be slower uphill and faster downhill.

needs.title: Roundabout approach and movement

source_cards.front: What is the rule for rotary definition?
source_cards.back: A rotary connects roads from several directions around a central island and normally has yield controls at the entrances.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for rotary direction?
source_cards.back: Traffic moves counterclockwise around a rotary.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for rotary entry yielding?
source_cards.back: Yield to pedestrians and traffic already in a rotary unless signs or an officer direct otherwise.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for rotary exit signal?
source_cards.back: Signal as at other intersections and use the right-turn signal when leaving a rotary.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for single lane rotary?
source_cards.back: For a single-lane rotary, enter from the approaching road’s right lane and leave into the destination road’s right lane.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for posted rotary lane choice?
source_cards.back: At a multilane rotary, follow lane-choice signs when provided.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for short rotary route?
source_cards.back: Without lane-choice signs, a quarter-turn or straight movement uses the right lane into and through the rotary and exits to the right lane.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for long rotary route and exception?
source_cards.back: Without lane-choice signs, a three-quarter-turn or U-turn uses the left entry and an inner or middle rotary lane before exiting right, except that entry from a single-lane road stays in the right lane throughout.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for rotary lane change?
source_cards.back: Do not change rotary lanes until it is safe because traffic may be on either side.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for missed rotary exit?
source_cards.back: After missing a rotary exit, go around again when safe and position for the proper exit rather than stopping in the rotary.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for roundabout entry?
source_cards.back: Choose a roundabout lane using approach signs and apply the rotary’s entry and lane-selection rules.

needs.title: Sharing lanes and space with bicycles

source_cards.front: What is the rule for reserved areas?
source_cards.back: Do not park in a bicycle lane, taxi stand or posted loading zone.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle full lane right?
source_cards.back: Bicyclists may use the full lane even when a bicycle lane exists, except on a limited-access or express state highway with signs prohibiting bicycles.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle right side pass?
source_cards.back: A bicyclist may keep right while passing a motor vehicle traveling in the lane.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle signal exception?
source_cards.back: A bicyclist signals a turn or stop with either hand but may omit or interrupt the signal when both hands are needed for safe operation.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for side by side bicycling?
source_cards.back: No more than two bicycles may travel side by side, and on a multilane same-direction road they must remain in one lane without unnecessarily preventing a pass.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle parking?
source_cards.back: A bicycle may be parked on a road or sidewalk only without obstructing vehicle or pedestrian travel.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle large vehicle hazard?
source_cards.back: Bicyclists should give large vehicles room, avoid their blind spots and never pass a moving tractor-trailer on the right.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for no abrupt right hook?
source_cards.back: Before turning right after passing a bicycle, allow safe distance from the rider and use a reasonable proper turning speed.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for patient bicycle pass?
source_cards.back: If a lane is too narrow to pass a bicycle safely, wait for room in an adjacent lane or a safe passing opportunity and keep at least four feet clear.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for protected bicycle lane?
source_cards.back: A separated bicycle lane physically divides bicycle traffic from motor traffic and may use green bicycle markings across an intersection.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for pedestrian lane separation?
source_cards.back: Pedestrians must stay on the sidewalk rather than in a bicycle lane.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for look for bicycles before crossing?
source_cards.back: Before turning across a bicycle lane, check for approaching bicycles, including looking beside and behind the vehicle when needed.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for protected lane bicycle duties?
source_cards.back: Bicyclists must use the proper lane direction, continue through the intersection in the lane while watching for turns and yield to crossing pedestrians.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for hidden bicycle awareness?
source_cards.back: Drivers must watch for bicycles hidden by vehicles or buildings and avoid underestimating a bicycle’s speed or the space needed to pass it.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for door zone rule without lane dependence?
source_cards.back: Keep at least three feet from parked cars when bicycling whether or not a bicycle lane is present.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle box location?
source_cards.back: A bicycle box is a green bicycle-marked area before the crosswalk that spans the travel lane and helps riders position for a turn at red.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for left position in bicycle box?
source_cards.back: A bicyclist making a left turn from the box should move to its left side, signal and wait for green.

source_cards.front: What is the rule for two stage bicycle turn?
source_cards.back: For a two-stage bicycle left turn, first cross straight on green into the destination road’s bicycle box, then wait for that road’s green before crossing straight again.

source_cards.front: What does the manual state about the Drive Out bicycle crash scenario?
source_cards.back: Drive Out is one of the manual's common motor-vehicle-and-bicycle crash scenarios in which the motorist is at fault, while bicyclists can improve visibility by riding farther left in the lane.
